Overall, we believe that Helen Keller's coverage surveys are designed to measure key indicators of the success of VAS campaigns and to achieve samples that are generally representative of target populations. Helen Keller’s surveys use an audit procedure whereby supervisors re-survey a random sample of participants, and Helen Keller has increasingly begun to report the results from this procedure. This alleviates some of our initial concerns about the quality of Helen Keller's auditing procedure and gives us more confidence in the accuracy of the monitoring data. However, we note that the caregiver-reported nature of responses may produce bias in results. 

For more information on our analysis of Helen Keller’s monitoring, see our grantee review here: https://www.givewell.org/charities/helen-keller-international#Methodology/

rows.label: Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
